text:
arjun: Heads up — after landing ar/opt-compressor warmup (PR #712) we see a small tail-latency regression on long-seq workloads. P95 up ~8% for seq=1024, batch=4. Attached nsys and perfetto captures. Anyone seen this locally?
leah: I can repro on canary. Not huge but noticeable on our R1 tests. p50 unchanged, tail moves.
tomas: Quick glance at nsys timeline: there's an extra cudaMemcpyAsync-ish spike between the compressor kernel and the KV-apply kernel. It looks like a memcpy fence around 00:00:12.
arjun: exact timestamps from my run: memcpy spike starts at 12.345s, lasts ~0.9ms, then kernel reenqueue. nvprof shows additional host->device copies labeled as `compressor::spill`
rachel: @arjun link to the captures?
perf-bot: nsys capture uploaded: https://perf.redwood/internal/3101234567/nsys-archive.zip (sizes: before=120MB after=140MB)
leah: I ran a before/after diff (before = commit 9e8c1a, after = PR #712 merge). perfetto flame shows a small band of memcpy right after warmup pass.
mike: quick hypothesis: warmup introduced a temporary staging buffer/serialize step to ensure deterministic compression order. That could trigger a memcpy if buffer lifetime moved to host.
tomas: here's the exact CLI I used to repro:```
nsys profile -o run.nsys --trace=cuda,osrt --force-overwrite --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi ./bench --seq 1024 --batch 4
```
arjun: thanks. I also captured a perf script that lists device->host events:```
# simplified perf excerpt
12.345678: memcpy H2D size=256K tag=compressor:spill
12.346789: kernel compressor_main
12.347900: memcpy D2H size=16K tag=kv_apply:meta
```
rachel: Can someone do a quick bisect to confirm the regression intro point? If it's PR #712 we should consider reverting the warmup tweak or gate it behind a flag.
mike: I started a narrow bisect spanning 9e8c1a..712beef, running a small CI harness that samples p95 over 10 runs. First failing commit is 5f3a2d1 (looks like a refactor of compressor buffer ownership).
arjun: nice. 5f3a2d1 shows a change from device-only allocator to hybrid allocator that sometimes pins a staging buffer on host. That matches the memcpy.
leah: quick experiment: forcing allocator to prefer device-only for the compressor removes the memcpy and tail goes back to baseline. Verified on 2/2 runs.
tomas: low-effort patch: in warmup path, pass `Allocator::DeviceOnly` to compressor init. I have a draft CL: https://codereview.redwood/CL/9876 — keeps warmup but avoids staging.
arjun: do we have concerns about OOM/regression in memory usage? Warmup intentionally avoided device-only earlier to reduce OOM risk.
mike: yeah tradeoff. But we can make it heuristic: DeviceOnly for seq>=512 and batch<=8; otherwise fallback. That would cover our long-seq workloads.
rachel: sounds reasonable. Add a telemetry counter for `compressor_alloc_mode` so we can monitor.
perf-bot: perf regression alert muted for canary; follow-up job queued: https://ci.redwood/runner/3101234567/compare (runs: before/after, 20 iters each)
leah: FYI I also ran a microtrace with nvtx ranges around the warmup and saw the memcpy present only in the merged branch. Attaching a short log snippet:```
[warmup] init compressor -> allocate hybrid buffer
[memcpy] host->device 256K
[compressor] warmup pass
[kv_apply] kernel
```
arjun: plan: short-term revert-of-allocator-change in warmup unless patch from Tomas passes internal mem/oom checks. Long-term: add allocator heuristics + telemetry + an automated perf test for warmup path.
mike: I can own the telemetry + CI perf test. Tomas can own CL to prefer device-only on long-seq. Rachel can review rollback if needed.
arjun: thanks all. Please post results from the CI compare here when ready. I'll keep the captures linked in the ticket: https://tickets.redwood/INC-4592
perf-bot: CI compare finished: before p95=62.1ms, after p95=67.0ms, delta=+7.97% (n=20).
leah: CI confirms. Will open revert PR if Tomas' CL doesn't land by EOD. :hourglass:
